description.text: Flavio Anicio Ermogeniano Olibrio was a Roman senator from the aristocratic Anicii family, the son of Anicia Faltonia Proba and Sesto Petronio Probo, a prominent consul in 371. He shared the consulship of 395 with his brother Flavio Anicio Probino, a young pair whose joint office was celebrated in a panegyric by Claudio Claudiano, indicating that they were raised in Rome and were still very young at the time.

Both Olibrio and his brother were Christians, a notable fact given their family's traditional pagan aristocratic background. Their appointment as consuls was likely a deliberate signal by Emperor Theodosius I following the restoration of paganism under Emperor Flavius Eugenius. They were honored with a dedication of the work Exempla elocutionum by Arusianus Messianus and received a letter from Quintus Aurelius Simmacus. Olibrio married his relative Anicia Giuliana and had a son and a daughter, Demetria.

curiosities.text: A panegyric by Claudio Claudiano was specifically dedicated to the consulship of Probino and Olibrio, underscoring their prominence and youth.
Olibrio and Probino were among the first Christian consuls in the late Roman Empire, reflecting Theodosius I's policy shift.
The work Exempla elocutionum by Arusianus Messianus was dedicated to Olibrio and Probino, indicating their patronage of rhetorical literature.
Olibrio's marriage to Anicia Giuliana produced a daughter named Demetria.
